In summary, our research is concerned with

a new and interesting aspect of P. aeruginasa quorum sensing that has never been reported before, i.e. the emergence of LasR-deficient mutants in stationary-phase cultures of the non-mutS parental strain.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

mutS inactivation in P. aeruignosa leads to the emergence of a specific colony variant with a nonfunctional LasR and that, under the conditions of the present study, this variant has an advantage over the wild type.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the emergence of the mS2 morphological variant in the mutS background is the consequence of a selective process that favours a LasR-deficient strain.
mutS mutants are able to generate new phenotypes, including the emergence of LasR-deficient variants, which could have important implications in the ecology of this opportunistic pathogen.
